prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
[goal] Reconstruct the June game-server outage from `./logs` and record start, end, duration, availability, SLO status, and root cause in `./result.json`.

[action] Parsed the three daily logs (`gameserver-2026-06-01/02/03.log`) plus `logs/README.md`; grepped for ERROR/FATAL/WARN; isolated the single incident on June 2 and wrote `./result.json`.

[result] Incident ran `2026-06-02 03:17:42` -> `03:53:31` (35.82 min). June availability 99.9171%, which clears the 99.9% monthly SLO (allowed 43.2 min; used 35.82 min), so `slo_999_ok = true`. Root cause: `/data` disk exhaustion (97% used, 3.1 GB free) -> `SaveGame failed: No space left on device` -> server unresponsive -> watchdog loop of exit-code-137 restarts until backup rotation freed 38.2 GB at 03:52:10, then `server ready, accepting players` at 03:53:31.

[next] Nothing further requested; report is complete.

How I know it's right: the window endpoints are byte-exact lines from `gameserver-2026-06-02.log` (`ERROR SaveGame failed ... No space left on device` at L251 03:17:42 and `INFO server ready, accepting players` at L294 03:53:31), matching README's definition of down ("first save error" to "'server ready'"). Duration is simple wall-clock difference (35 min 49 s). Availability uses README's stated 30-day June (43,200 min): (43,200 − 35.82)/43,200 = 99.9171%. No other gaps in heartbeat coverage exist across the three files, consistent with README's "there is only one incident." All numbers recomputed and re-checked against the source lines before writing.
